prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds revealed in
earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only tells you how often this line type was paid at all.
- If you decide the line is indemnified and no cap, sub-limit or percentage reduction applies,
  take the stated amount as t and give a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. These
  amounts are before such policy arithmetic; apply caps and reductions on top.
- A line type that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies
  do not carry; price it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 10 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 2 of 6 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 38 (80% range 32 to 45); revealed per hr: 35-42 (case 24), 35-40 (case 26), so this line (4 hr) about 152 (129 to 181)
- line 17 "Administrative and claim-processing fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 5 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary removal of leak residue from affected surfaces. Allow €65 gross for cleaning the utility-room floor only.
The hallway was reached by the escaping water, so necessary residue removal is covered under §7.1.7(h). Allow €80 gross for the affected floor area.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that it no longer leaks, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. Allow €95 gross for a straightforward inspection.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(a) and 5.2.1 cover removal and disposal of the damaged fixed trim. Allow €95 gross for a modest removal and disposal job.
Fixed skirting is a building component under §4.2.2. Allow €230 gross for like-for-like supply and fitting on the damaged runs only under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in a separate room with no established damage from the leak.

items.description: Measure moisture in both affected floors
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) expressly covers necessary moisture measurements. Allow €165 gross for the survey of the utility room and hallway, consistent with Case 21.

Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying in the two affected spaces. Allow €105 gross for drying services distinct from rental and separately billed labour, subject to the duplicate-cost exclusion in §7.1.8(c).
Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary equipment hire. Allow €55 gross for short-term rental if it is not already included in the drying charge under §7.1.8(c).
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary labour not already priced into earlier lines under §7.1.8(c). Four hours at the calibrated €38 gross per hour gives €152.

items.description: Measure and dry unaffected basement storage room
items.rationale: There is no documented leak damage in the basement storage room. Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude extending drying measures to a separate unaffected room.
Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport, but only from the balance after restoration takes priority against the €1,190 gross per-item cap. If a balance remains, allow up to €100 gross for the trip.
Section 5.2.6 covers the assessment only to the extent the €1,190 gross cap remains after restoration and the preceding transport line. Allow €135 gross if sufficient headroom remains.

Section 5.2.6 covers drying and stabilisation, but this line receives only what remains of the €1,190 gross cap after restoration, transport and assessment. Estimate €120 gross conditional on a positive residual.

The affected, professionally assessed painting qualifies under §5.2.6 despite the general contents exclusion. Full restoration is likely to exhaust the unscheduled-item limit and has first priority: €1,000 net × 1.19 = €1,190 gross.
Section 5.2.6 applies only to an item affected by the insured event, and the second painting was unaffected. The general contents exclusion in §4.3(d) therefore applies.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separately charged administrative, handling and processing fees. The fee is also not a conservation measure under §5.2.6.
